4. The defendant opposite party No. 1 entered appearance in OC Suit No. 68 of 1986 and accepted all liabilities in respect. of the house and executed a solenama with the plaintiff and the suit was disposed of in terms of the solenama. The terms were that the defendant-opposite party No. 1 would accept all the liabilities and do everything to have the execution of the sale deed completed by the plaintiff-petitioner. 

 11. It is further submitted that the implications of non-payment of the House Building Finance Corporation loans and dues by the defendant opposite party No. 1 as per terms of the power of attorney and solenama have not been properly considered by the courts below. He argues that the non-payment of instalments amounts to misconduct on the part of defendant No. 1 for which both the power of attorney and solenama are liable to be cancelled by the Court. 

 15. Here in this case the plaintiff has admitted to have entered into an agreement to sell the property to the defendant No. 1 and acknowledged the receipt of part consideration and executed power of attorney in favour of the latter as a result a relationship of principal and agent between the plaintiff petitioner and the defendant opposite party No. 1 has been created by a contract. Incident of that contract are to be governed and determined by provisions of Contract Act 1872. The Act does not allow revocation of an authority where the agent's authority is coupled with interest. The agent has paid Taka 95,000.00 to the principal as part consideration before the power of attorney has been executed and then again paid several installments to the House Building Finance Corporation. Ext. 'Chha' series are the receipts according to which an amount of Taka 50,000.00 was paid to the defendant opposite party No. 2 by the defendant opposite party No. 1 by instalments. An examination of the solenama Ext. 'G' shows that a further amount of Taka 45,000.00 was paid to the plaintiff-petitioner by the defendant opposite party No.1 before signing of the solenama. That being so, existence of interest of the defendant opposite party No. 1 in the suit land can well be evidenced. We also do not find evidence that the defendant opposite party No. 1 has failed to pay all the instalments to the House Building Finance Corporation. Therefore, it cannot be maintained that the conduct of the defendant opposite party No. 1 merits the revocation of the power of attorney. 

 17. Therefore, we are of the opinion that the defendant-opposite party No. 1 has beneficial interest in the disputed house which forms the subject matter of the power of attorney inasmuch as it is agreed to be sold by the plaintiff petitioner to the defendant-opposite party who had paid substantial amount of money as consideration to the plaintiff towards the purchase price at the time of the execution of the agreement, the power of attorney and the solenama and got into possession and, as such, the power of attorney cannot, therefore, be revoked by the plaintiff petitioner in view of section 202 of the Contract Act
